name: Nancere
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Only Jungraithmayr 1977 wordlist-level citation surfaced; no phonology with stress located online

tone_statements.citation: Peust, Carsten. 2018. The subgrouping of East Chadic. Folia Orientalia 55: 235-253. doi:10.24425/for.2018.124686
tone_statements.quote: NA: Nancere, 81 000 speakers (2007). Main source: Hamm (2002: 23–27)6. The documentation of this language is weak, but I decided to include it in this study because it is the largest of all East Chadic languages. I also cull a few words out of the Nancere New Testament translation (Ogekob Ku Herua), citing book and verse number in a footnote. Tones of this language have not been researched and cannot be indicated.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 238-239, section listing the languages and main sources (entry 'NA'); the '6' after '23–27' is footnote marker 6 ('In that source, all verbs are cited along with the 3rd sg. masc. subject proclitic ba-, which will be omitted here.'); footnote 5 on p. 238 gives the tone diacritics used for the other languages.
tone_statements.summary: No tone system stated: author reports Nancere tone is unresearched and cites Nancere data without tone marks (other East Chadic languages in the paper carry L/M/H/falling/rising marks).

sources.citation: Hamm, Cameron. 2002 [2003]. Sociolinguistic survey of the Kabalay language of Chad. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2003-008.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Says Nancere 'has already been developed to some extent (with a written Bible)' and was the reference language for RTT and a 225-item wordlist (Appendix D, no transcription notes); cites Barreteau 1978:304 and Jungraithmayr 1981:410 for classification only; no Nancere phonology in its references.

sources.citation: Gouffé, Claude. 1978. Linguistique tchadique. Annuaire de l'École pratique des hautes études, IVe section, 1977-1978: 249-292 (Persée search hit for 'nancere').
sources.note: Nothing. Seminar report on comparative Chadic person/gender/number marking; Nancere appears only in language listings; no phonological statement.

sources.citation: Hoffmann, Carl. 1971. On the classification of Nancere. Journal of West African Languages 8(1): 5-12.
sources.note: Nothing. Read in full (8 pp., scanned, scanned). Classification paper whose Nancere data are 'entirely taken from the New Testament in Nancere' (1969); gender linkers ku/te/ka, pronoun sets, numerals, ~30 lexical cognates; no phonology, no tone, no stress. Its bibliography is the only place naming a description of a Nancere variety: 'Lamy (Lami?), Pierre. (No date.) Etude succincte de la langue lélé et du dialecte Nantchoa. Beyrouth: Imp. Miss. Cath. (Not seen.)' (p. 12).
Nothing; en page cites only Ethnologue (dialects Mire, Bolo, Kwale); fr page is a village list with no bibliography.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann & Dymitr Ibriszimow. 1994. Chadic Lexical Roots. 2 vols. (Sprache und Oralität in Afrika 20). Berlin: Dietrich Reimer.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Contains tone-marked Nancere (Béré) lexical data from Jungraithmayr's 1970s field notes (Marburg Chadic Word Catalogue); its introduction gives per-language source and transcription notes, the closest thing to a published phonological statement for Nancere.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann. 1979. Apophony and tone in the Afroasiatic/Niger-Congo frontier area. Études linguistiques (Niamey) 1: 130-140.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Glottolog's only phonology-relevant reference for Nancere (language code Miltu, Nancere, Gabri); built on Jungraithmayr's own Nancere (Béré) field data; would at least state whether Nancere is tonal and how tone interacts with the word.

sources.note: Orthography proposals covering nangjere among Chadian languages (Google Books snippet shows 'tonale' discussion); a practical-orthography report typically states whether tone/accent needs marking for each language.

sources.citation: SIL Tchad / Alliance Biblique du Tchad unpublished Nangjere materials (orthography guide, lexicon, Bible-translation notes), N'Djaména; Nangjere NT 1974 (Brotherton, Foyer de la Bible), Bible 1986; Martin Waingué served as Nangjere consultant for Wiesemann, Sadembouo & Tadadjeu 1983, Guide pour le développement des systèmes d'écriture des langues africaines.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only modern first-hand phonological work on Nangjere was done for Bible translation and orthography; the SIL library in N'Djaména holds such grey literature (cf. Hamm 2002:7 for Kabalay). OLAC/SIL catalogues could not be reached to confirm what exists.

sources.citation: Tucker, A. N. & M. A. Bryan. 1966. Linguistic Analyses: The Non-Bantu Languages of North-Eastern Africa. London: Oxford University Press for the International African Institute. (Somrai group, p. 161 ff. per Hoffmann 1971)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number 2235.4.26; Linguistics Library, call number CoPh 36.88); only the abstract or an excerpt is openly accessible
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number 2235.4.26; Linguistics Library, call number CoPh 36.88
sources.note: Their group sketches carry short 'Tone'/'Stress' notes drawn from sources such as Lami; unverified whether Nancere itself is analysed (Hoffmann cites p. 161 only for group membership).

sources.citation: Lami, Pierre (with Jean Bakko [and Kaifnat]). 1942. Étude succincte de la langue lélé et du dialecte nantchoa. Préface du Général de Larminat. Beyrouth: Imprimerie Catholique (Documents d'Ethnologie africaine). 197 pp. (Glottolog) / 296 pp., 5 maps, 3 pl. (Bibliographie du Tchad 1968 record).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only grammatical description of a Nancere variety (the Nantchoa/Nancoa dialect) ever published; a French colonial-era sketch of this kind normally has a section on 'accent'/'tons'. Cited by Hoffmann 1971 as 'not seen'; Glottolog files it under Lele.

sources.citation: Catalogue searches: Crossref, HAL, theses.fr, DOAJ, BnF catalogue SRU, Gallica SRU, SUDOC, Library of Congress, OpenLibrary, archive.org metadata, local HathiTrust hathifile, local ASJP sources (Nancere list = Hoffmann 1971 + Lukas 1937), local WALS (Nancere absent)
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: All negative: no thesis, article or book on Nancere/Nangjere/Nantchoa in any of these; BnF and SUDOC have no record containing the words nancere, nangjere or nantchoa (so Lami 1942 is not yet obtained/digitised there); hathifile has no Lami 1942 and Tucker & Bryan 1966 is not in it either.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid nanc1253 (page + BibTeX of its 8 references); Glottolog full-text bibliography searches for nancere / nangjere / nandjere / nantchoa
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Glottolog's most extensive description for Nancere is 'wordlist'. The 8 refs are Bruel 1905, Gaudefroy-Demombynes 1907, Lukas 1937, Cabot 1965, anon. 1976 'Eléments pour une orthographe pratique des langues du Tchad', Hoffmann 1971, Jungraithmayr 1979 'Apophony and tone..' (11 pp., description type unknown), Hamm 2002. Full-text search 'nantchoa' returns Lami, Pierre 1942, Étude succincte de la langue lélé et du dialecte nantchoa, Beirut: Imprimérie Catholique, 197 pp., listed by Glottolog as a grammar sketch, assigned to Lele [lln] (ref id 17065). No phonology of Nancere exists in Glottolog.
